# nish/json-equal

whether two JSON values are equal by JSON Schema's rule, a canonical text and a hash that agree with it, and the first repeated element of an array, which is what `const`, `enum` and `uniqueItems` ask.

```ts
import {
  jsonEqual,
  jsonEqualCanonical,
  jsonEqualFirstDuplicate,
  jsonEqualHash,
} from "nish/json-equal";
```

```ts
import { jsonEqual, jsonEqualFirstDuplicate } from "nish/json-equal"

const doc = new JsonDocument(new JsonLimits())
const a = doc.parseText('[{"x":1,"y":[true]},{"y":[true],"x":1.0}]')
jsonEqual(doc, doc.at(a, 0), doc, doc.at(a, 1))   // true
jsonEqualFirstDuplicate(doc, a)                    // 1
```

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="jsonEqual" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#jsonequal">

Whether value `a` of document `da` equals value `b` of document `db` by JSON Schema's rule (the module header): numbers by value, objects whatever their member order.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="jsonEqualCanonical" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#jsonequalcanonical">

The canonical text of value `v`: the same text for exactly the values `jsonEqual` calls equal, so it is a key for a `Map` or `Set` of values.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="jsonEqualFirstDuplicate" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#jsonequalfirstduplicate">

The position of the first element of array `v` equal (`jsonEqual`) to an earlier one, or `-1` when every element is distinct or `v` is not an array: JSON Schema's `uniqueItems` holds exactly when this is `-1`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="jsonEqualHash" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#jsonequalhash">

A 64-bit hash of value `v` that agrees with `jsonEqual`: equal values hash the same.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="The rule">

Two values are equal when they are the same kind and: two
numbers have the same mathematical value (`1`, `1.0` and `1e0` are equal;
`nish/json-number` decides, never through `f64`), two strings have the
same string, two booleans the same value, two arrays the same length and
equal elements in order, and two objects the same keys with equal values,
in whatever order the members are written. `null` equals only `null`, and
`true` is not `1`. A number whose exponent is past
`JSON_NUMBER_MAX_EXPONENT` cannot be read exactly, and equals only a number
written with the same text.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**No depth limit.** Every walk keeps its own stack in an array, so a tree
built with `push` and `set` deeper than any parser allows compares as well
as a flat one, and nothing recurses.

</scalar-callout>

<scalar-detail title="What a call costs">

`jsonEqual` stops at the first difference. Up to
there it is linear in the values' size, except that each pair of objects
reads every key (one string each) and sorts them, `n log n` for `n`
members; it also allocates one string per string value, its stack, and
whatever `jsonNumberCompare` allocates per number pair. `jsonEqualCanonical`
builds the canonical text, about the size of the value written as JSON,
and sorts keys the same way. `jsonEqualHash` is FNV-1a of that text's
units: its bytes natively, its code units under Node. Every order and
length below is in those units too.
`jsonEqualFirstDuplicate` makes the canonical text of every element up to
the first repeat and keeps them in a `Map`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The hash is not keyed">

FNV-1a (public domain) is the same in every
process, so an attacker can make many values that share a hash, and a
table keyed by `jsonEqualHash` alone degrades to a list. It is for a
filter or a fingerprint; `jsonEqualFirstDuplicate` keys its `Map` by the
canonical text, which the `Map`'s own keyed hash spreads.

</scalar-detail>

## jsonEqual

Whether value `a` of document `da` equals value `b` of document `db` by
JSON Schema's rule (the module header): numbers by value, objects whatever
their member order. The two may be one document. `false` when either
handle names no value. Iterative, so any depth compares.

```ts
function jsonEqual(
  da: JsonDocument,
  a: i32,
  db: JsonDocument,
  b: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="da" type="JsonDocument" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="a" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="db" type="JsonDocument" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="b" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">
</scalar-field>

## jsonEqualCanonical

The canonical text of value `v`: the same text for exactly the values
`jsonEqual` calls equal, so it is a key for a `Map` or `Set` of values. It
is not JSON: each value is a tag and what it holds, `z`, `t` and `f` for
null, true and false, `n` and a `jsonNumberCanonical` text and `;` for a
number, `s`, a length, `:` and the string itself, `a` and a count and `:`
before an array's elements, and `o` and a count and `:` before an object's
members in key order, each key a length, `:` and the key (orders and lengths
as the module header says).
`""` for a handle that names no value.

```ts
function jsonEqualCanonical(
  doc: JsonDocument,
  v: i32,
): string
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="doc" type="JsonDocument" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="v" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">
</scalar-field>

## jsonEqualFirstDuplicate

The position of the first element of array `v` equal (`jsonEqual`) to an
earlier one, or `-1` when every element is distinct or `v` is not an array:
JSON Schema's `uniqueItems` holds exactly when this is `-1`. Linear in the
elements read, through a `Map` of their canonical texts.

```ts
function jsonEqualFirstDuplicate(
  doc: JsonDocument,
  v: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="doc" type="JsonDocument" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="v" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">
</scalar-field>

## jsonEqualHash

A 64-bit hash of value `v` that agrees with `jsonEqual`: equal values hash
the same. FNV-1a of the canonical text's units (its code units under
Node, so a string past U+00FF hashes differently there), unkeyed (the
module header says what that means for a table). The offset basis for a handle that names no
value.

```ts
function jsonEqualHash(
  doc: JsonDocument,
  v: i32,
): u64
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="doc" type="JsonDocument" required>
</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="v" type="i32" required>
</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u64">
</scalar-field>
